source: Order adapted from the Daily Turkish deck: each lemma of its ranked list (itself adapted from the 2018 Turkish list of FrequencyWords by Hermit Dave, CC BY-SA 4.0, built from the OpenSubtitles2018 corpus) was matched by meaning to its usual Turkmen equivalent, then edited by hand: film-dialogue words dropped or moved down, Turkish lemmas that share one Turkmen word merged, everyday Turkmen words added where their use would put them. Ranks are an editorial estimate, not a Turkmen corpus count. The ranked list is scripts/turkmen/tm-wordlist.tsv (CC BY-SA 4.0); method in turkmen/TM-PROJECT.md 7.8. Glosses, examples and notes are original.

cards.note: As **a, an** it comes before the noun: *bir kitap* (a book). Turkmen has no word for **the**.
On its own, *Bolýar* means **OK**. In tenses where "to be" needs a verb, it is *bolmak*: *Ertir öýde bolaryn* (I'll be at home tomorrow).
Written **attached** to the word it questions: *gelýärsiňmi?*, *dälmi?* *-my* after back vowels, *-mi* after front vowels.
Its case forms start with m: *muny* (this, as an object), *muňa* (to this), *munda* (in this). Plural *bular* (these).
Dative *maňa* (to me), genitive *meniň* (my), accusative *meni* (me). Needed with the future in *-jak*, which has no personal ending: *Men geljek*.
Dative *saňa*, genitive *seniň* (your). Use *siz* with strangers and older people.
No gender: *ol* is **he**, **she** or **it**. Dative *oňa*, genitive *onuň*, accusative *ony*. Before a noun, **that**: *ol jaý* (that building).
*Näme üçin?* (why?).
After a pronoun it is often contracted: *menem* (me too), *senem*. *Hem … hem* means **both … and**.

ex.en: Aýna and Merdan are at school.

cards.note: *Hem-de* (and also) joins longer phrases.
t becomes d before a vowel and before *-ýär*: *edýär*, *eder*. It builds many compound verbs: *kömek etmek* (to help), *jaň etmek* (to call).

ex.en: I bought lots of things at the market.

cards.note: *Bir zat* (something), *hiç zat* (nothing), *hemme zat* (everything).
Pronouns before it take the genitive: *meniň üçin*, *seniň üçin*. *Näme üçin?* (why?), *şonuň üçin* (so, that's why).
Another verb before it stays in the infinitive: *gitmek isleýärin* (I want to go).

ex.en: Is there any bread at home?

cards.note: With a possessed noun it means **to have**: *Meniň maşynym bar* (I have a car). The opposite is *ýok*.

en: not (with nouns, adjectives and the future)
cards.note: Negates nouns, adjectives and the future in *-jak*: *talyp däl*, *geljek däl*. Other verb forms take *-ma/-me*.
Nouns after it stay singular: *köp adam* (many people). **Very** before an adjective is *örän* or *gaty*.
*Hoş geldiňiz!* (Welcome!) is its past tense.
After a verb in *-yp* it means **can**: *Ýüzüp bilýärin* (I can swim). *Bilmeýärin* (I don't know).

ex.en: I'd like to, but I don't have time.

cards.note: *Emma* also means **but**, a little more formal.
t becomes d before a vowel and before *-ýär*: *gidýär*, *gider*, *gidip*. For going to a place, *barmak* is also common.
Also an adverb: *gowy gürleýär* (speaks well). *Gowy görmek* means **to like**.
t becomes d before a vowel and before *-ýar*: *aýdýar*, *aýdar*. *Aýdym aýtmak* (to sing).
Literally **in this place**. Also *şu ýerde* (right here); *bu ýere* (to here), *bu ýerden* (from here).

ex.en: I bought bread at the market.

cards.note: *Satyn almak* says **to buy** more precisely. *Alyp gelmek* (to bring).
Also the everyday **no**: *Ýok, sag bol* (No, thanks). With a possessed noun, **not to have**: *Wagtym ýok* (I have no time).
The polite imperative *beriň* with a dative is a common way to ask for something.
*Bu näme diýmek?* (What does this mean?). *Diýip* introduces quotes and reasons.
Makes comparatives: *has uly* (bigger). The thing compared takes *-dan*: *Batyr Myratdan has uzyn* (Batyr is taller than Myrat).
Takes the dative: *maňa seret*. t becomes d before a vowel and before *-ýär*.
*Gowy görmek* (to like). After a verb in *-yp*, **to try**: *Okap gör* (try reading it).
*Şu wagt* (right now).
Takes the dative: *agşama çenli*, *Aşgabada çenli*. *-dan … -a çenli* is **from … to**.
Comes after its noun: *ejesi ýaly* (like her mother).
Dative *bize*, genitive *biziň* (our).
The present tense of *bolmak*, used as **OK**. *Bolýarmy?* asks **Is that OK?**

ex.en: I have a lot of work.

cards.note: *Işe gitmek* (to go to work), *işde* (at work). *Işlemek* (to work) is built on it.
The plural **you**, and the polite **you** for one person. Dative *size*, genitive *siziň* (your).
*Her gün* (every day), *her hili* (all kinds of).
*Olaryň biri* (one of them).
Literally **for what**. The answer often starts with *sebäbi* (because).
Written in lowercase, as an adjective and a noun: *türkmen dili* (the Turkmen language), *türkmençe* (in Turkmen). The country is *Türkmenistan*.
*Ýagdaýlaryň nähili?* (How are you?).

ex.en: How do I get to the market?

cards.note: Asks how something is done; *nähili* asks what something is like.
With possessive endings it means **-self**: *özüm* (myself), *özüň* (yourself), *özi* (himself, herself).
Always written with a hyphen.
Points closer than *bu*, or at what was just mentioned. Accusative *şuny*.

ex.en: That day I wasn't at home.

cards.note: Points back to something already known: *şol adam* (that man, the one we talked about).
*Gijä galmak* (to be late).
*Şeýle-de bolsa* (even so).

ex.en: There are many people at the market.

cards.note: After numbers and *köp* the noun stays singular: *köp adam*. *Adamlar* (people).
*Pikir* is a thought or an opinion. *Öýtmek* also means **to think**, in the sense of **to suppose**.
With *-dan* it means **after**: *nahardan soň* (after the meal).
*Bu ýerde* (here), *ol ýerde* (there).

en: to go out, to come out

ex.en: She went out of the house.

cards.note: Where from takes *-dan*. *Durmuşa çykmak* (to get married, of a woman).
Also **right away**: *Häzir gelýärin!* (I'm coming!).
*Hiç haçan* (never). As a conjunction, *haçan-da* (when).

ex.en: My father works at the hospital.

cards.note: The e of the stem becomes ä before *-p*, *-r* and *-n*: *işläp*, *işlär*, *işlän*.
The person who needs takes the dative: *Maňa suw gerek* (I need water). *Gerek däl* (no need).

en: not at all, never (with a negative)
cards.note: Always with a negative verb or *ýok*: *hiç kim* (nobody), *hiç zat* (nothing), *hiç haçan* (never).
*Nirä* (where to), *nireden* (where from).
Dative *olara*, genitive *olaryň* (their).
*Gürleşmek* (to talk with someone, to chat).
What you think comes first, with no word for **that**: *Gelýär öýdýärin* (I think he's coming).
Makes superlatives: *iň uly* (the biggest), *iň köp* (the most).
*-dan öň* means **before**: *işden öň*. After a span of time, **ago**: *bir ýyl öň*.
Genitive *kimiň* (whose).
Plural *çagalar*. *Çagalyk* (childhood).
*Öýe* (home, to the house), *öýde* (at home), *öýüm* (my house). *Ak öý* is the white felt yurt.
Nouns after numbers stay singular: *iki kitap*.

ex.en: I go to school every day.

cards.note: Also **sun**: *Gün dogdy* (the sun rose). *Şu gün* (today).
*Kakam* (my father). *Ata* is **grandfather**.
*Ol ýere* (to there), *ol ýerden* (from there).

ex.en: I didn't understand, please say it again.

cards.note: Takes the dative: *saňa düşünýärin* (I understand you).
*Azajyk* also means **a little**.
*Gyz dogan* (sister).
**Son** is *ogul*: *oglum* (my son).
After a verb in *-yp*, an action done for good or in advance: *ýazyp goý* (write it down).

ex.en: My mother is cooking at home.

cards.note: *Ejäm* (my mother), *ejäň* (your mother): the final e becomes ä before these endings.
*Sag boluň* to someone you call *siz*; *köp sag boluň* (thank you very much). Literally **be healthy**, so it also works as **goodbye**.

ex.en: Do you have any other questions?

cards.note: *-dan başga* means **apart from, except**: *senden başga* (except you).
For things you like, *gowy görmek* or *halamak* is more usual.
What you like takes the accusative: *çaýy gowy görýärin*.
Who or what you wait for takes the dative: *saňa garaşýaryn*.

ex.en: I'll come tomorrow, that is on Saturday.

cards.note: **Arm** is *gol*.

ex.en: Life in the village is calm.

cards.note: *Durmuşa çykmak* (to get married, of a woman).
*Yza gaýtmak* (to come or go back).
t becomes d before a vowel and before *-ýar*: *gaýdýar*. *Gaýdyp gelmek* (to come back).
After a verb in *-yp* it marks an ongoing action: *garaşyp dur* (is waiting).
Literally **I make a request**. *Haýyş etmek* (to ask for).
*Ana* points further away: **there it is**.
*-yň içinde* (inside): *öýüň içinde*.
t becomes d before a vowel and before *-ýär*: *eşidýär*, *eşider*.
*Ak ýol!* (Have a good trip!).
The verb takes *-sa/-se* anyway; *eger* only stresses the condition.

ex.en: I didn't come because I was ill.

cards.note: Comes after the main clause and introduces the reason. Literally **its reason**.
Also the locative of *ol*: *Kitap onda* (He has the book).

ex.en: I don't live here any more.

cards.note: *Häzir* is **right now**; *indi* is **now, from now on**.
*Ýeke-täk* (the only one).

ex.en: The old dog died last year.

cards.note: **Straight ahead** is usually *göni*.
*Gijäňiz rahat bolsun* (good night). *Gijä galmak* (to be late).
k becomes g before a vowel: *kömegiň üçin* (for your help). *Kömek etmek* (to help) takes the dative: *saňa kömek edeýin* (let me help you).
What you start takes the dative: *işe başlamak* (to start work).
Takes the dative: *öýe girmek* (to go into the house).
Opposite: *aňsat* (easy).
*Başlamak* (to begin) comes from it.
*Dostluk* (friendship). *Jora* is more casual.

ex.en: My older brother lives in Mary.

cards.note: Of people, **older**: *uly doganym* (my older brother). *Has uly* (bigger).

ex.en: I don't have any money on me.

cards.note: The currency is the *manat*.

ex.en: Bring me a bowl of tea.
How many languages do you know?

cards.note: *Türkmen dili* (the Turkmen language), *ene dili* (mother tongue).

ex.en: There's a garden between the two houses.

cards.note: *-yň arasynda* (between): *iki öýüň arasynda*.

ex.en: I was in Ashgabat last year.

cards.note: *Täze ýyl* (New Year), *indiki ýyl* (next year).

ex.en: I went to the market with my mother.

cards.note: Written as a separate word: *awtobus bilen* (by bus). Pronouns before it take the genitive: *meniň bilen* (with me).

ex.en: The weather's bad, let's stay home.

cards.note: Opposite: *gowy*.
Takes a negative verb: *Hiç kim bilmeýär* (nobody knows).
*Aýalym* (my wife). *Zenan* is a more formal word for **woman**.
*Elmydama* means the same.
Its vowel is long, so t becomes d before a vowel: *adym, adyň, ady*. Not *at* (horse), with a short vowel: *atym* (my horse).
*Täze ýyl* (New Year), *täze çörek* (fresh bread).

ex.en: All the pupils are in the classroom.

cards.note: Comes before a noun: *ähli adamlar*. On its own, use *hemme*.
*Hemme zat* (everything), *hemme ýerde* (everywhere).

ex.en: I use a computer every day.

cards.note: *Salam aleýkim* is the fuller greeting. *Salam* fits any time of day.
*Gök çaý* (green tea) is the everyday drink, poured into a *käse* (bowl); *gara çaý* is black tea.

ex.en: I don't know the exact time.

cards.note: Takes the dative: *saňa ynanýaryn*.
The person asked takes *-dan*: *ondan sora* (ask him).
This question, literally **how are your circumstances?**, is the everyday **How are you?**
Polite and formal.

ex.en: What's the topic of today's lesson?

cards.note: k becomes g before a vowel: *mowzugy*.
*Ilkinji gezek* (the first time).
*Sagat bäşde* (at five o'clock), *iki sagat* (two hours).

ex.en: There are many languages in the world.
The child is drawing a picture.

cards.note: *Surat çekmek* (to draw; to take a photo), *çilim çekmek* (to smoke).
*-yň ýanynda* (next to, with): *öýüň ýanynda*.

ex.en: My little brother goes to school.

cards.note: Of people, **younger**. *Kiçijik* (tiny).

ex.en: My father has a new car.
I asked my mother for permission.

cards.note: Comes after the quote or thought it introduces.
*Özüňi nähili duýýarsyň?* (How do you feel?).

ex.en: This is a real Turkmen carpet.
I play football with my friends.

cards.note: Casual; *dost* is the general word.
*Bilmek* is to know a fact; *tanamak* is to know a person or a place.
*Hakda* means the same: *seniň hakda* (about you).
*Azajyk* (a little bit). Opposite: *köp*.

ex.en: There are five people in our family.

cards.note: Used after numbers: *üç kişi* (three people).
**To forget** is *ýatdan çykarmak*.

ex.en: The wedding went on for three days.
Buy two loaves of bread at the market.

cards.note: k becomes g before a vowel: *çöregi*, *çöregim*. Turkmen bread is baked in a clay *tamdyr*.

ex.en: The teacher explained the new words.

cards.note: From *düşünmek* (to understand): literally **to make understand**.
Written as two words. *Şu günki* (today's).

ex.en: The key is on the book.

cards.note: *-yň üstünde* (on), *-yň üstüne* (onto).

en: to meet, to see each other
cards.note: *Görüşeris!* (See you!) is a common goodbye.
Both **to finish** something and **to come to an end**: *Işimi gutardym* (I finished my work).
Takes the dative: *oňa garşy* (against him).
*Suwsuz* (without water).

ex.en: This is a very important issue.

cards.note: A university student is a *talyp*. From *okuw* (study).
*Öwretmek* is **to teach**.
*Gyz dogan* (sister). An older brother is *aga*, an older sister *uýa*, a younger brother or sister *jigi*.
Literally **to take out of memory**.
